# dsh-client-ui-font-scale

A DeepSeek Harness **client (browser) plugin**
that puts conversation font-size controls where you a

re already looking: a stepper in the composer
tool row, keyboard shortcuts, and `Ctrl`+wheel zoom.

No build step. The `lib/*.js` files are authored directly in the shipped bundle format, so cloning
t
he repository is enough.
## Why this exists

DSH already ships a conversation font-size setting — **Settings → General → 字号大小 / Font size**,
cont

ributed by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-theme`. Its copy is explicit that it *"only affects
conversat
ion content"*, which is exactly the right scope.
This plugin does not replace or reimplement it. It adds the input surfaces that setting lacks:

- reaching it takes four clicks, so it is easy to forget it exists;
- there is no keyboard shortcut

for it anywhere in the shipped shortcuts registry;
- there is no wheel gesture for it.
Every control here writes through the **same** `theme.setFontSize('text', px)` entry point the shipp

ed
row uses, so the two can never disagree.
## What it does
| Surface | Where | Behaviour |
| Stepper | composer tool row, before the submit action | `A−` / readout / `A+`, clamping at the end

s |
| Reset | beside the stepper | `↺` restores the default; greys out when already there |
| Shortc

uts | `Ctrl`+`=` / `Ctrl`+`-` / `Ctrl`+`0` | increase / decrease / restore default |
| Zoom | `Ctrl`
+wheel over the page | wheel up enlarges, wheel down shrinks |
Both the readout and the reset button render the **live** size from the theme snapshot, so a change
made in the shipped settings row updates this control immediately, and vice versa.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web client (the `desktop` profile, or any profile mounting
`@deepseek-ai

/dsh-web-app`).
- A theme service that exposes `setFontSize(role, px)` — i.e. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-clie

nt-ui-theme`,
which ships in the default composition. **DSH 0.2.1 or newer**: that release split the

single font
size into the `text` / `code` / `terminal` roles, and this plugin drives `text`.
- No b
uild step and no runtime dependencies beyond the browser module table.
## Install

This package is a **dsh bundle**: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so dsh treats
`cordis.
patch.yml` as a composition layer and mounts it for you.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That installs the package into the profile and appends it to the profile's bundle list. The profile

is watched, so dsh recomposes without a restart. Remove it with
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> remo
ve dsh-client-ui-font-scale`.
### From a local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Mounting by hand

Compose `cordis.patch.yml` into the profile's own patch file, and make the
package resolvable from t
he profile directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A patch `insert` row may also name a path instead of a package — dsh rewrites `./`-relative and
abso
lute names to file URLs anchored at the patch file — which needs no install at all.

After installing, **reload the page**: a client plugin's bundle is wired into the index at render
ti
me, so a page that was already open does not pick up a newly installed bundle.
## Persistence
This plugin stores nothing, deliberately.

`theme.setFontSize('text', px)` writes through the `ui-theme` settings scope on the Host
(`this.host

.set('fontSize', px)`), and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-theme`'s Host half re-embeds that
durable va
lue into **every index render** as a boot script. The result:
re the shell mounts*, so there is no flash of the default size.
A second store here would be a second source of truth for one number. If you want to change how the
size persists, change it in `dsh-client-ui-theme`, not here.
## Range

The accepted range is **10–22 px in whole steps**, default **14**. That range belongs to the theme
s

ervice: `setFontSize` throws for a fractional or out-of-range value. Every control here clamps
rathe
r than bypassing it, so the shipped settings row and this plugin always agree.

If you need to go beyond 22 px, note that `dsh-client-ui-layout` writes the size as an
*unimportant

inline* `--dsh-content-font-size` on `<body>`, so a stylesheet rule with `!important`
can override i

t. Doing that from a plugin means owning the resulting split-brain with the shipped
setting, which i
s why this plugin does not.
## How it works
| Concern | Mechanism |
| Seat | `ctx.slots.register` into `conversation.input.right` (a list slot, `replaceRisk: none`, emp

ty in the default composition) |
| Read | `theme.getTheme().fontSizes.text`, re-rendered on the `the

me/change` event |
| Write | `theme.setFontSize('text', px)` — the only font-size write entry |
| Ke
ys | `ctx.shortcuts.register`, so bindings appear on the Shortcuts settings page and stay user-rebin

dable |
| Locale | `ctx.locale.register` + `ctx.locale.bind`; the readout and labels follow the acti

ve locale |
| Styles | one `<style>` element inserted in `ctx.effect`, removed on dispose |
### The font-size API changed in DSH 0.2.1

Before that release the theme service carried one `fontSize` and `setFontSize(px)` wrote it. Since
t

hen the snapshot is `fontSizes: Record<'text' | 'code' | 'terminal', number>` and the write is
`setF

`fontSizes: Record<'text' | 'code' | 'terminal', number>` and the write is
`setFontSize(role, px)`.
This plugin had been written against the old shape, and the mismatch failed in a way worth recording
because it produced no visible error surface:
[该节后续省略]
## Caveats

- The control is a decoration in the composer row, not a settings replacement. The shipped
**Setting

s → General → Font size** row remains the canonical place to see and set the value.
- `Ctrl`+wheel c

alls `preventDefault`, which suppresses the Electron shell's own page zoom. That is
intentional — th

e gesture should mean one thing — but it does mean `Ctrl`+wheel no longer zooms
the whole page.
- Th

e wheel handler is attached to `window`, so the gesture works anywhere over the page, not only
over
the conversation column.
